svg.title: UVs, seams and unwrap: from a marked edge to a texture map
svg.desc: Seams are edges marked as cuts. Unwrap (smart) groups faces into charts by direction and projects each flat. Unwrap along seams lays each piece cut out by the seams flat with least squares conformal maps. Both pack the pieces into the 0 to 1 square with one common scale and store a UV per point in the mesh (format version 3). The map is used by the UV checker, the UV window with a stretch view, and GLB export. Tools that do not know UVs remove the map and say so.
svg.text: UVs, seams and unwrap (Phase 13, step 8)
A UV map says where each point of the surface lies on a flat texture, like a sewing pattern for the surface.
1. Seams (optional)
Mark seam / Clear seam on
selected edges; drawn red.
Outline selects a lid's rim.
2. Unwrap (two ways)
Unwrap: one button, needs no seams
Along seams: careful, keeps angles
both replace any earlier map
3. Packed map
one scale for all pieces,
2% margin, in 0 to 1
equal texture sharpness
4. Stored
u, v for every point
in the mesh (v3)
seams stored too
Unwrap (smart): charts and projection
1. Charts: grow from the biggest face; a neighbour joins while it points
within 66 degrees of the chart's average. Seams are never crossed.
2. Project each chart flat along its average direction (real size).
3. Turn the long side across, one common scale, shelf packing by bisection.
4. A point used by two charts is split in two (same place, own UV).
Always works. A little distortion on curved surfaces. The shading is
averaged across split points (under 40 degrees) so the cuts do not show.
packages/shared/src/unwrap.ts
Unwrap along seams: conformal maps
1. Pieces: faces joined without crossing a seam. A closed piece is
refused: "mark seams to cut it open".
2. Wedges: a spot cut by a seam becomes two vertices (one per side).
3. Solve (LSCM): two far border points held, the rest by conjugate
gradient. Angles are kept, so a texture does not shear.
4. Right winding, real area, turned along its long axis, packed.
A piece that cannot lie flat (a ring with no cut) still gets a map; the
turned-over faces are counted and shown red. Up to 60 000 triangles.
packages/shared/src/lscm.ts
Example: a can, cut open
lid and base: a seam round each rim
(select the lid, Outline, Mark seam)
the side: one seam down its length unrolls it into a rectangle
How stretched a face is
even
stretched
the worst of: shape change (circle to ellipse),
size change against the average, turned over.
uvStretch in lscm.ts; the UV window's Stretch mode
What uses the map
UV checker: a checkerboard per object
UV window: click, drag, turn, scale, pack
GLB export: written as TEXCOORD_0
Edits change the map only, one undo each. Next:
painting and baking (step 10), textures (Phase 4)
What other tools do with the map (wrong UVs are worse than none)
Kept: moving points (the surface moves, the map does not); Bend, Twist, Taper, Stretch, Noise; Mirror, Array and Thicken copy it;
Divide and Loop cut interpolate it; Extrude, Inset, Bevel, Fill hole copy or average it; Delete, Merge and Weld renumber it.
Dropped, with a message: only Smooth, for now (it merges points that share a spot, which a UV seam cannot survive).
New walls of an extrusion are smeared until you unwrap again (red in Stretch). Seams ride along like creases. Format version 3.
